label: sequence started with w: late original steps (t>=7) and <DEL>
explanation: Fires almost only in sequences whose first original token is w (93% of activation mass), at the late end of the input: original positions 6-8 and the <DEL> step (t = 6..9), and never in the copy phase. Activation grows across the late original positions. It peaks on the last original token (to_go = 0) and is somewhat lower on <DEL>. So it shows up mostly in long sequences (L = 8-9); in L = 7 sequences it is usually silent on <DEL>. It does not fire before t = 6, does not depend on the identity of the current input token, and fires only weakly at the end of sequences that do not start with w. Predicate (first token w, t >= 7, not copy phase): dev precision 0.80, recall 0.75, mass recall 0.92. Most missed steps are weak activations.

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong for L=8. The explanation says activation 'peaks on the last original token (to_go = 0) and is somewhat lower on <DEL>'. That holds only for L=9. Within first_tok==w sequences on dev: L=8 t=7 (last original) has precision 0.78 and mass 0.111, while L=8 t=8 (<DEL>) has precision 0.92 and mass 0.159, so <DEL> beats the last original token there. L=9: t=7 is 0.77/0.106, t=8 (last original) 0.99/0.283, t=9 (<DEL>) 0.99/0.230. The peak follows absolute step t=8, not to_go=0. Firing reads as a ramp in absolute time over steps 7..L, which is consistent with by-t (t=8 holds 50% of mass) and by-L (L=9 holds 69% of mass).

Most of the L=7 behaviour checks out. For w-start L=7, t=7 (<DEL>) has precision 0.35, so it is mostly silent, and t=6 has precision 0.08. Dropping L=7 gives test P 0.886, R 0.697, F1 0.780, against the original's test P 0.798, R 0.748, F1 0.772. That matches the claimed trade-off. Calling the L=7 <DEL> step the source of 'most false positives' overclaims, though: test misses also show inactive or weak steps in L=8 (e.g. t=7 inactive), and L=8 t=7 contributes about 22% false positives.

The factual claims that check out: zero activation in the copy phase (by-phase copy = 0 of 2.7M steps); no firing before t=6; first_tok==w holds 93% of activation mass; little dependence on in_tok (largest lift 1.6x, for f).

Missed activations (about 25% of active steps, 8.4% of mass on test) are diffuse weak firing in sequences that do not start with w, at t>=7 and L=9. I found no systematic class behind them. Candidates tested: orig(1)==w gives precision 0.06; first_tok in {n,t,c,k} at L9 t8 gives precision 0.12; in_tok==f gives precision 0.18. Treating these as noise is reasonable, so the verdict stays 'explained'. The failed point is the specific magnitude claim.
